The fed funds rate is 2.45%, which points to a period between December 2018 and mid-2019. The 10-year yield at 2.54% and the 2-year at 2.30% fit April 2019 or possibly May 2019. Other readings also fit this window:

- US large-cap equity is up 12.1% over 3 months with no drawdown, which suggests a new high. That fits April 2019, after the rebound from the December 2018 low.
- Unemployment of 3.8% matches March/April 2019. April was 3.6%, while March was 3.8%.
- Headline CPI at 1.86% fits March 2019, which was 1.9%. Core CPI at 2.04% also fits March 2019, which was 2.0%.
- Fed funds at 2.45% is consistent with March 2019, which was 2.41%. The March 10-year yield was 2.41%, though, and the 2-year was about 2.27%.
- The 10-year at 2.54% with a 1-month change of -0.5% on 7-10y Treasuries fits April 2019, when the 10-year was 2.50%.
- The 10y-2y spread of 0.24 fits April 2019.

The payrolls 3-month average of 180k fits April 2019, which was about 169k. The 12-month dollar change of +5.56% fits April 2019 as well.

The 3-month equity return of 12.1% fits end of April 2019 (Feb–Apr). The 1-month return of 4.1% matches April 2019, which was 4.0%. Treasuries fell 0.5% in the month, which also matches April. I settle on April 2019.
